## Steering-group recommendation — 23 November 2026
Status: private draft for review, not a decision or authority to contract. Consolidates F14–F18 and the assessment in item:bcb6269e-76bf-4fb4-8a01-1e645f8cba64; supersedes the 16 November recommendation where inconsistent.

### Customer-service impact
Approximately 300 weekly calls concern order status and prices combined [F14]. Customers should be able to see order status themselves. Butikkskyen has the better evidenced integration starting point; Composa's longer integration path risks delaying benefits. Neither has demonstrated Northwind order-status self-service, price visibility or call reduction. No staffing savings are claimed. Fram commerce remains excluded.

### Recommended course
Proceed with Butikkskyen as preferred platform and Kodeverket as proposed build partner, subject to validation and commercial checks before commitment. This is a qualitative recommendation on the four current criteria, not an agreed weighted score. Standard Dynamics 365 connector, updated pricing capacity and stronger reference timing favour A; marketing usability is unproven for both A and B.

For one store, A's 450,000 NOK annual licence plus Kodeverket's 1.1M fixed build offer gives 1.55M NOK in year one and 2.45M over three years. Against the revised 2.0M first-year budget, 450,000 NOK remains before unquoted costs. B is ~3.5M in year one, ~1.5M over budget, and ~5.3M over three years, assuming the 800,000 integration estimate is additional to its 1.8M build. These are licence/build subtotals, not full TCO.

Northwind's 3,100 price lists fall below Butikkskyen's vendor-stated v4 capacity of 10,000 [F15–F16]. The old 2,000-list workaround is historical; demonstrate current-version performance and near-real-time prices/stock rather than carrying it forward as a blocker.

1. Demonstrate 3,100 price lists, near-real-time Dynamics 365 sync, order-status self-service, customer prices, part-number search and quick reorder; test marketing workflow.
2. Confirm written fixed-price scope/integration coverage, one-store licence, yearly cancellation, exclusions and all remaining first-year costs within 2.0M NOK.

Proposed steering decision: endorse A as preferred, agree the approval gates and accountable owners, and confirm who may authorise contract commitment after the gates pass. # Steering-group presentation outline — draft, 23 November 2026
Private working draft; not shared or approved. Prepared from recommendation item:bcb6269e-76bf-4fb4-8a01-1e645f8cba64 and findings F1–F18 on page:1d46ebfc-5ef6-496c-9987-bd0b65a626a0. Cost-bearing material must be sent to Northwind only via procurement portal, never email.

## 1. Customer service: make order status and prices self-service
- About 300 calls/week concern order status and prices combined [F14]; customer service wants customers to see order status themselves.
- A: stronger integration starting point, but order-status and price self-service need demonstration. B: longer integration path risks delaying benefits.
- Neither option has proven call reduction; baseline avoidable calls before claiming savings.

## 2. Recommendation: proceed conditionally with Butikkskyen
- Preferred platform A, with Kodeverket as proposed build partner; not an unconditional contract approval.
- Better evidence on speed, lower licence/build subtotal and standard Dynamics 365 connector.
- Customer-service capability, marketing workflow, complete costs and delivery remain approval gates.

## 3. Decision frame: four criteria and clear constraints
- Criteria: time to market; three-year cost; Dynamics 365 fit; marketing usability. Weights/scoring unagreed; speed is Gunnar's stated priority.
- Shop target: 1 September 2027; revised year-one budget: 2.0M NOK [F18].
- Near-real-time prices/stock, customer-specific pricing and two-person integration team constrain delivery. Fixed build/yearly licence cancellation requested by procurement.

## 4. Shortlist: Butikkskyen against Composa
- A: standard connector and included B2B Pricing app; four-month reference launch, not a Northwind promise.
- B: custom integration, estimated four months before shop work; nine-month reference launch and integration overrun. Greater schedule/integration risk.
- Marketing usability unverified for both. C already dropped: commerce-module support ends December 2028; website CMS unaffected.

## 5. New evidence removes the old pricing-capacity concern
- Northwind has 3,100 customer-specific price lists [F15], distinct from its ~4,000 parts.
- Vendor says B2B Pricing v4 supports up to 10,000 lists without the old workarounds [F16]. Do not use the historical 2,000-list threshold as the current limit.
- Validate Northwind's lists and near-real-time sync on v4; vendor capacity statement is not measured performance.

## 6. Economics: 450,000 NOK remains before unquoted costs
- A: annual licence 450,000 + fixed build 1.1M = year one 1.55M; three years 2.45M NOK [F12,F17]. One-store assumption.
- B: year one ~3.5M, ~1.5M over revised budget; three years ~5.3M NOK [F7,F11]. Assumes 800,000 integration is additional to 1.8M build; overlap unconfirmed.
- A build cost increases 200,000; budget falls 500,000; headroom falls from 1.15M to 450,000 NOK.
- Licence/build subtotals, not full TCO: establish hosting, support, operations, escalation, exclusions and tax treatment.

## 7. Delivery: commit to a plan, not a reference date
- Get Kodeverket's capacity, milestones, integration responsibilities, testing and acceptance plan against 1 September 2027.
- Four-month reference does not justify promising an April 2027 Northwind launch.
- Sequence proposed: commercial/technical validation, build and integration, user testing, pilot, launch. Dates need partner commitment.

## 8. Approval gates: close the gaps before contract commitment
- Demo order status, correct customer prices, 3,100 lists, near-real-time prices/stock, part-number search and quick reorder.
- Demonstrate marketing workflow; confirm operating workload for the integration team.
- Confirm fixed-price scope/integration, one store, yearly cancellation, full year-one affordability and delivery commitments.
- Proposed contributors, not assigned owners: Hanne for customer service; Ola for technical validation; Lise for commercial checks; marketing representative for content workflow.

## 9. Decision requested and next steps
- Endorse Butikkskyen as preferred, subject to gates; agree accountable owners and who may authorise commitment after validation.
- Kodeverket offer expires 15 December 2026 [F17]; confirm steering date and complete checks in time or seek extension.
- If a material condition fails, return to steering group; do not automatically select Composa or reopen C.
- Send cost-bearing decision material through procurement portal only.

## 2026-11-23 Draft recommendation: commerce platform (for Ana's review; not a decision)
### Customer service
F14 establishes about 300 calls/week about order status and prices, and a desire for self-service order status. The split between query types and achievable call reduction are unknown. A: demonstrate authenticated order status and correct customer pricing; F15–F16 remove the earlier stated 2,000-list limitation as a current vendor-reported barrier, but do not prove Northwind performance. B: order-status self-service is also unverified; custom integration creates a potential support burden, not a measured effect. C remains dropped; no further implementation assessment is recommended. Do not claim 300 calls/week will disappear or that any option already provides order-status integration.
### Recommendation
Continue to recommend A — Butikkskyen, conditionally. F16 strengthens pricing-scale evidence and F17 supplies a fixed-price build offer. No platform selection has been made. B remains outside budget and has weaker schedule evidence; C was dropped by agreement with Gunnar on 16 November because support ends December 2028.
### Cost
A: Kodeverket fixed-price build 1.1M [F17] + 0.45M annual one-store licence [F12] = 1.55M NOK year 1; 1.1 + 3×0.45 = 2.45M over three years. Against the reduced 2.0M cap [F18], quoted-scope headroom is 450k, not an allowance proven sufficient for remaining work. Confirm that F17 includes connector implementation, pricing, order-status work, migration, training and other necessary scope; avoid double counting. One-store sufficiency and written licence scope remain open. These figures exclude unpriced operations, taxes, increases and contingency.
B: year 1 is 3.5M if F11's 800k integration is additional to the 1.8M build, or 2.7M if included; respectively 1.5M or 0.7M above the new cap. Three-year baselines remain 5.3M or 4.5M. Do not reopen B without a materially revised price and credible schedule.
### Pricing scale
Northwind has 3,100 price lists [F15]. Butikkskyen says version 4 supports 10,000 and removes earlier workarounds [F16]. Treat F9's 2,000-list issue as historical rather than a current product limit. Require a version-4 demonstration using Northwind's actual pricing rules, permissions and representative load; capacity is not proof of near-real-time D365 integration.
### Delivery and offer deadline
Kodeverket's offer expires 15 December 2026 [F17], potentially before a late-December steering-group decision. Obtain a committed resource plan and schedule, and either decide in time or secure a written extension. Four months from a December start suggests April 2027 only as a reference-based scenario, not a partner commitment. Deadline remains 1 September 2027; coordinate with the 1 March website launch.
### Conditions before contract
1. Demonstrate near-real-time D365 prices AND stock, version-4 pricing for 3,100 lists, and authenticated order-status self-service, including exception handling and ownership.
2. Confirm fixed-price scope, exclusions, partner availability and committed dates; include all required work inside the 2.0M first-year cap.
3. Obtain written one-store licence scope and annual cancellation terms. F17 meets the fixed-price-offer gap, not all procurement conditions.
4. Demonstrate marketing's required same-tool workflow, quick reorder and part-number search.
5. Agree support, training and operational ownership with Hanne and Ola. Establish baseline call categories and success measures; no quantified savings yet.
The four scored criteria remain time to market, three-year cost, D365 fit and marketing ease of use; weights are unset. Customer service is an opening impact section, not an automatically added scored criterion.

6. Decide in time for the 15 December offer expiry or obtain a written extension. Do not accept an inadequately validated offer solely to preserve the price.

texts.text:
## Customer-service implications

F14 gives us a concrete baseline: **about 300 calls a week about order status and prices**, plus a clear request for self-service order status.

- **Butikkskyen:** demonstrate customer-visible order status and correct customer-specific prices. The earlier pricing-workaround concern is substantially reduced by F16, but neither order-status integration nor actual call reduction is proven.
- **Composa:** the same self-service capabilities remain unverified; its custom integration adds potential support and exception-handling work.
- **Fram:** remains dropped, rather than a live alternative.

We should not assume all 300 calls can be eliminated.

## Updated recommendation

**Butikkskyen remains the strongest conditional recommendation.** F15–F17 strengthen its case, although the reduced budget leaves less room for omissions.

| Cost baseline | Butikkskyen | Composa |
|---|---:|---:|
| First year | **1.55M NOK** | 2.7–3.5M NOK |
| Three years | **2.45M NOK** | 4.5–5.3M NOK |
| Against new 2.0M first-year cap | **450k remaining** | 700k–1.5M over |

Butikkskyen now uses the **1.1M fixed-price build**, replacing the earlier 900k estimate, plus the existing 450k annual one-store licence. These remain quoted-scope baselines, not complete TCO.

### What changes
- **Pricing scale:** Northwind’s 3,100 lists fall below version 4’s vendor-stated 10,000-list capacity. The old 2,000-list workaround is historical evidence—not a current product limit. Still require a demonstration with Northwind’s actual pricing rules and D365 data.
- **Procurement:** a fixed-price build offer is now available. Scope, exclusions and yearly licence cancellation still need confirmation.
- **Decision timing:** **the offer expires 15 December**, potentially before a late-December steering-group decision. Secure an earlier decision or written extension; do not accept solely to preserve the price.
- **Delivery:** April 2027 remains a reference-based scenario, not Kodeverket’s committed date.

The key remaining checks are order-status self-service, near-real-time D365 prices **and** stock, complete fixed-price scope, licence terms, marketing workflow and a committed delivery plan.

Saved F14–F18 and updated the private [draft recommendation](item:0b2bc674-1b29-40b2-8748-ac74d156f923) and [comparison](item:994f8b00-38eb-40da-9519-5369417312ff). I also added a private follow-up for **11 December** to resolve scope, schedule and offer expiry.

Updated the [recommendation](item:0b2bc674-1b29-40b2-8748-ac74d156f923) and saved the [presentation outline](item:4129b055-2563-41ee-91a6-407340ed8a3a), both as private drafts.

## Updated recommendation

**Proceed with Butikkskyen and Kodeverket as the preferred route, subject to validation and contract conditions—not unconditional approval to sign.**

The latest findings strengthen the pricing-scale evidence and provide a fixed-price build offer. The revised baseline is **1.55M NOK in year one and 2.45M over three years**, leaving **450k against the reduced 2.0M first-year cap**. Complete scope, self-service order status, D365 performance, licence terms and delivery commitments still need confirmation.

## Steering-group presentation — 10 slides

### 1. Customer service: the case for self-service
- About **300 calls a week** concern order status and prices; customer service wants customers to see status themselves. [F14]
- Butikkskyen must demonstrate status visibility and correct customer pricing. Composa has the same unverified capabilities, plus potential custom-integration support work. Fram is already dropped.
- Establish the call-category split and success measures; do not assume all 300 calls will disappear.

### 2. Recommendation: progress Butikkskyen with Kodeverket
- Best remaining combination of delivery evidence, quoted cost and standard D365 integration.
- Version 4 pricing evidence and a fixed-price build offer strengthen the case.
- Seek endorsement of the preferred route, with contract signature conditional on the remaining checks.

### 3. Requirements and decision criteria
- Spare-parts shop live by **1 September 2027**, within a **2.0M NOK first-year budget**.
- Four criteria: time to market, three-year cost, D365 fit and marketing ease of use. Speed is Gunnar’s priority; weights remain unset.
- Required capabilities include customer-specific pricing, near-real-time prices and stock, quick reorder, a fixed-price build and yearly-cancellable licences.

### 4. What the new findings change
- **F14–F15:** a concrete customer-service baseline and **3,100 customer-specific price lists**.
- **F16:** vendor reports that B2B Pricing v4 supports **10,000 lists without the previous workarounds**.
- **F17–F18:** **1.1M NOK fixed-price build**, valid until **15 December**; first-year budget reduced from 2.5M to **2.0M NOK**.

### 5. Pricing scale and D365: stronger evidence, validation still needed
- Northwind’s 3,100 lists fall within the vendor-stated v4 capacity; the old 2,000-list workaround is historical, not a current vendor-reported limit.
- Test actual pricing rules, customer permissions and representative load—not just list count.
- Demonstrate near-real-time D365 **prices and stock**, and validate order-status integration separately.

### 6. Financial case: within budget on the quoted scope
- **Year one:** 1.1M build + 450k annual licence = **1.55M NOK**; remaining headroom **450k**.
- **Three years:** 1.1M + 3 × 450k = **2.45M NOK**.
- This is not complete TCO: confirm scope, one-store sufficiency, operations/support, migration, training, taxes, increases and contingency.

### 7. Why not Composa or Fram commerce?
- Composa costs **2.7–3.5M NOK in year one**, depending on whether the integration estimate is included in the build: **700k–1.5M above budget**.
- Its four-month integration precedes shop work; the nine-month reference and integration overrun weaken schedule confidence. Maintenance also burdens the two-person team.
- Fram commerce was dropped because support ends in December 2028. Marketing’s same-tool requirement remains unverified for both remaining options.

### 8. Delivery: protect September; do not promise April
- Shop deadline remains **1 September 2027**; coordinate resources with the **1 March website launch**.
- A four-month reference suggests April only as a scenario from an immediate December start—not Kodeverket’s commitment.
- Obtain a scoped delivery plan, resources and testing milesto

### 9. Conditions before contract signature
- Prove pricing accuracy, permissions, near-real-time D365 data and authenticated order-status self-service.
- Confirm complete fixed-price scope, first-year affordability, licence scope, annual cancellation and committed delivery dates.
- Demonstrate marketing workflow, quick reorder and part-number search; agree training, support and operational ownership.
- **Third-party dependency:** the B2B Pricing app.

All other slides remain unchanged.

**Recommend Butikkskyen (A) with Kodeverket as build partner, conditionally.** This is your private draft, not a decision, and nothing has been shared (item:a8e497ae-b370-4732-9a60-5a9c992f924b).

## Why Butikkskyen
- **Cost:** A is about 1.55M NOK in year one and 2.45M over three years. That leaves 450k NOK of the 2.0M budget before costs not yet quoted.
- **Composa (B)** is about 3.5M in year one, roughly 1.5M over budget, and about 5.3M over three years.
- **Dynamics 365:** A has a standard connector and an included pricing app. B needs a custom integration.
- **Speed:** A has a reference customer that launched in four months. Speed is Gunnar's top priority.
- **Pricing capacity:** Northwind has 3,100 price lists. The vendor says version 4 handles up to 10,000.
- All figures are licence plus build, not full TCO. They assume one store.

## Rejected options
- **Fram CMS commerce module (C):** Gunnar agreed on 16 Nov to drop it. Fram's support for the module ends in December 2028, and Fram recommends moving to a partner platform. Its cheap three-year figure ignores a migration. Dynamics 365 fit and timing were never verified. The website CMS itself is not affected (page:fb5f11ed-01da-471a-b8ba-8f11a202d104).
- **Composa (B):**
  - Ola estimates 800k NOK and four months of custom integration before shop work can start. That is an estimate, not a quote, and I assumed it is additional to the 1.8M build.
  - Its reference customer took nine months and the integration overran.
  - It is the weakest on time, cost and integration, and has no edge on the active criteria. Reopen it only for a much cheaper, committed integration offer.
  - Your 9 Nov lean towards Composa predates this evidence (item:22c5cc38-422c-45ad-b6ff-36c40afa9740).

## Criteria
- The four current criteria are time to market, three-year cost, Dynamics 365 fit and marketing ease of use.
- **Weights and scoring are not agreed.** The ranking is qualitative and rests on "speed first".
- Customer-service impact is an extra analysis section requested by Gunnar, not a scored criterion.
- Procurement's needs (fixed build price, yearly-cancellable licences) and part-number ordering are not formally criteria or requirements.

## What changed since the first comparison
- **Criteria:** design flexibility was dropped on 9 Nov, after your call with Gunnar. Five criteria became four.
- **Option C:** dropped on 16 Nov (F13).
- **Composa:** F11 added the 800k integration and four months.
- **Butikkskyen cost:** the licence fell from 600k to 450k for one store (F12). The build rose from about 900k to a fixed 1.1M from Kodeverket (F17).
- **Budget:** cut from 2.5M to 2.0M (F18). Headroom on A therefore fell from 1.15M to 450k.
- **Pricing limit:** the 2,000-list workaround concern is no longer the vendor-stated blocker, with 3,100 lists against 10,000 on version 4 (F15, F16).
- **Customer service:** Hanne reports about 300 calls a week on order status and prices combined. She wants customers to see order status themselves (F14).

- **Unproven for A:**
  - Order-status self-service and correct customer prices.
  - Performance with 3,100 lists on version 4, and near-real-time prices and stock.
  - Part-number search, quick reorder and marketing's content workflow.
  - Call reduction. Don't claim that all 300 calls disappear.
- **Commercial:**
  - Kodeverket's written scope and exclusions.
  - The one-store assumption and yearly cancellation.
  - Full year-one costs within 450k, and partner capacity.
  - A committed plan for 1 Sep 2027. The "April 2027" go-live is an extrapolation, not a promise.
  - The B2B Pricing app is a third-party dependency.
- **Decision process:**
  - The steering date is unconfirmed in my records. The Kodeverket offer expires 15 Dec, so either decide before then or get an extension (task:07d09a21-2c96-4ad9-a78c-c3a594a6b258).
  - Gate owners and contract authority are not assigned.
  - Weights are unagreed.
  - Composa's cost overlap is unconfirmed.
- **Housekeeping:**
  - The second Composa reference task is still open, though it wouldn't change the assessment (task:3a9b946f-6f5d-40d1-b818-36d4685d42e1).
  - The customer-service-first rule proposal is still waiting for your decision (proposal:a7e4045d-8e22-4023-84b7-aa040afca564).
  - The validation task with Hanne and Ola is open (task:605fdfc6-44e3-4c6c-b22b-d3e67fe43bab).

## What to ask the group for
Endorse A as preferred, agree the approval gates and their owners, and say who can authorise the contract once the gates pass. If a gate fails, the matter returns to the group and does not default to Composa. The nine-slide outline is ready (page:4860b841-351c-416f-82e9-4c517721030d).

## Finding F19 — Composa with nightly import instead of custom integration (Ola Nordmann, 27 November 2026; Gunnar's question)
Option B Composa, follow-up to F11 and item:22c5cc38-422c-45ad-b6ff-36c40afa9740. Ola Nordmann says a nightly import of prices and stock would cost about 200,000 NOK instead of the 800,000 NOK custom integration [F11], but prices in the shop could be up to a day old. This is an estimate, not a Composa quote.

- **Cost (same basis as item:fbf86dc1-040f-4177-bbb3-81cf8177b1e8; licence + build, not full TCO; assumes the integration cost is additional to the ~1.8M build, overlap unconfirmed):** build + integration ~2.0M NOK (was ~2.6M); year one ~2.9M NOK (was ~3.5M), about 0.9M over the revised 2.0M budget [F18]; three years ~4.7M NOK (was ~5.3M). Still the most expensive option and still over the first-year budget. Butikkskyen with Kodeverket remains 1.55M year one, 2.45M over three years.
- **Requirement conflict:** every option was to read prices and stock from Dynamics 365 in near real time [F1, F3]. A nightly import does not meet this: prices up to a day old, and stock presumably as well, which could mean wrong prices or unavailable parts shown. Whether Northwind accepts day-old prices is a business decision (Gunnar, procurement, customer service) and is not established here.
- **Customer service:** day-old prices could add price-related calls, which are part of the ~300 calls a week [F14]. Not measured. Order-status self-service is not covered by F19.
- **Not established by F19:** the time to deliver the nightly import (F11's four months applied to the custom integration); whether it removes the custom-integration timing risk against 1 September 2027; ongoing operation by the two-person team; how customer-specific prices (3,100 price lists [F15]) would be handled in a nightly import.
- **Assessment:** F19 narrows B's cost gap but does not remove it, and trades the cost for a weaker fit with Dynamics 365. The draft recommendation (Butikkskyen preferred, conditionally) is unchanged; the draft and slides have not been updated for F19. Whether the view changes is for Ana and Gunnar to decide.

**We recommend Butikkskyen (A) with Kodeverket as build partner, as a conditional route.** The steering group would endorse the route, but nobody signs until the checks below pass. This is a draft recommendation, not a decision (item:0b2bc674…, item:994f8b00…).

## Why we recommend it
- **Cost:** Year 1 is 1.55M NOK and three years is 2.45M. That is a 1.1M fixed-price build plus a 450k annual licence for one store. It leaves 450k of headroom under the new 2.0M first-year cap.
- **Time to market:** This is the sponsor's top priority. Our one reference went live in four months, but that is not a Northwind commitment.
- **D365 fit:** A standard connector and the B2B Pricing app are included. The vendor says v4 handles 10,000 price lists, and Northwind has 3,100.
- **Procurement terms:** The build is fixed-price, which Lise wanted.

## Options rejected
- **Fram commerce module (C): dropped.** Gunnar agreed on 16 November because Fram ends support for it in December 2028. Its cheap 2.1M baseline left out a migration that would fall inside the three years.
- **Composa (B): not recommended, but I find no recorded decision to drop it.**
  - It is over the cap either way: 3.5M year 1 and 5.3M over three years if the 800k integration is extra, or 2.7M and 4.5M if it's included. That is 1.5M or 0.7M over.
  - Its custom D365 integration takes four months before shop work starts, and its reference took nine months with an integration overrun. Ola's two-person team would also have to maintain it.
  - The draft says Composa is not an automatic fallback.
- **Your own lean:** On 9 November you leaned towards Composa. That was before Ola's estimate, and the evidence no longer supports it. It is yours to reconsider.

## Criteria compared
1. Time to market
2. Three-year cost
3. Fit with Dynamics 365
4. Marketing ease of use

Weights are still not agreed, so there is no weighted score. Customer-service impact is the opening section of the pack, not a fifth scored criterion. Must-haves are customer-specific prices, near-real-time prices and stock from D365, reordering in a few clicks, a fixed-price build and yearly-cancellable licences.

## What has changed since the first comparison (9 November)
- **Criteria:** Design flexibility was removed on 9 November, going from five criteria to four. This also took away Composa's one strength.
- **Butikkskyen licence:** The 600k quote covered two stores. One store costs 450k.
- **Composa integration (F11):** Ola estimated 800k and four months, which moved Composa from 0.2M over the cap to over budget in both readings.
- **Fram:** Support ends in 2028, so it was dropped.
- **Customer service (F14):** Hanne reports about 300 calls a week on order status and prices, and wants customers to see order status themselves.
- **Price lists (F15, F16):** Northwind has 3,100. The vendor says v4 removes the 2,000-list workaround our reference needed.
- **Build cost (F17):** Kodeverket offers a 1.1M fixed price, up from the 0.9M estimate. The offer expires on 15 December.
- **Budget (F18):** The first-year cap fell from 2.5M to 2.0M.

## Still open
- **Technical proof:**
  - Test v4 pricing on Northwind's real 3,100 lists. So far we only have the vendor's claim.
  - Prove near-real-time D365 prices and stock.
  - Demonstrate authenticated order status for customers.
- **Kodeverket's offer:**
  - Get the full scope and exclusions, named staff and a committed schedule.
  - Confirm that order status, migration and training fit the 450k headroom.
  - Decide before 15 December or get a written extension. Don't accept an unvalidated offer just to keep the price.
- **Licence:** Get written confirmation that 450k covers one store and that one store is enough, plus yearly cancellation.
- **Marketing:** Neither option has shown that marketing can work in the same tool as the website, or that quick reorder and part-number search work.
- **Not a full cost yet:** Operations, support, tax, annual increases and contingency are not included.
- **Weights:** Agreeing them with Gunnar is still open. That task was due 27 November.
- **Composa F11:** We still haven't confirmed with Ola whether the 800k is on top of the 1.8M build. Composa fails the cap either way.
- **Customer service:**
  - The 300 calls aren't split by cause, and no savings are quantified.
  - We have no customer-service reference.
- **Delivery:** April 2027 is only an illustration from an immediate December start. The 1 September deadline has to be coordinated with the 1 March website launch.
- **Ownership:** Responsibilities are proposed but not agreed: Ola on technical checks, Hanne on service measures, Lise on scope, licence and extension, and you and Gunnar on coordination.
- **Third-party risk:** The B2B Pricing app is a third-party dependency. You asked for this on the risks slide only.

The steering-group deck (page:70884dff…) already follows this structure. I haven't changed anything.

## Comparison against four criteria — revised 30 November 2026, F1–F19
Assessment, not selection. Weights remain unset. Customer-service impact opens the recommendation but is not a fifth scored criterion. C was dropped on 16 November and is historical only.

Offer expires 15 December 2026 [F17]. | Custom integration takes four months before shop work [F11]; nine-month reference with integration overrun [F10]. A December start leaves little contingency before September 2027; do not add reference duration and integration duration without knowing overlap. |
| Three-year cost | 2.45M NOK = 1.1M fixed-price build [F17] + 3×450k licence [F12]. Year 1 1.55M; 450k headroom against new 2.0M cap [F18]. Scope and one-store sufficiency need confirmation. | 5.3M/3.5M over three years/year 1 if 800k integration is additional; 4.5M/2.7M if already included [F7,F11]. Year-1 overrun 1.5M or 0.7M. Nightly-import variant: see note below [F19]. |
| D365 fit | Standard connector and B2B Pricing included [F6]. Northwind has 3,100 lists [F15]; vendor reports v4 supports 10,000 without previous workarounds [F16]. Old 2,000-list limitation is historical; actual pricing rules, performance, near-real-time prices AND stock remain to be demonstrated. | Custom integration required [F11], substantial ownership burden for two-person team [F3]. Customer pricing and near-real-time data unverified. Nightly-import variant: see note below [F19]. |
| Marketing ease of use | Same-tool requirement and usability unverified; demonstrate. | Same-tool requirement and usability unverified; demonstrate. |
Customer-service baseline: 300 calls/week about prices and order status; self-service order status wanted [F14]. Neither A nor B has demonstrated it. No supported savings estimate.

### Note under Composa: nightly import instead of custom integration [F19]
Gunnar asked whether Composa would work with a nightly import of prices and stock instead of the custom integration. Ola (27 November): about 200k NOK instead of 800k, but shop prices could be up to a day old [F19].
- **Cost:** If the 800k was on top of the 1.8M build, year 1 becomes about 2.9M and three years about 4.7M (1.8M + 0.2M + licences), still about 0.9M over the 2.0M cap. If the 800k was already inside the 1.8M, year 1 was 2.7M; even if the full 600k saving came off the build (not stated) it would be about 2.1M, still above the cap. Either reading still exceeds 2.0M, and the cheapest reading is not evidenced. A's quoted year 1 remains 1.55M.
- **Requirement conflict:** The agreed must-have is near-real-time prices AND stock from D365 [F1,F3]. A one-day-old import does not meet it, so this variant needs Gunnar and Ola to relax the requirement explicitly (customer-specific prices and stock up to a day stale; consequences for orders and for order-status self-service [F14] not assessed). If the requirement were relaxed it would apply equally to A, which would then be easier to deliver as well.
- **Still unknown:** delivery time for the variant (four months in F11 applied to the full integration), whether 200k is a fixed price, and the remaining ownership/maintenance load for Ola's two-person team.
- **Effect on the assessment:** B gets cheaper but remains over budget on the evidence, and only by loosening a must-have. The recommendation of A is unchanged.

Cost figures are quoted-scope baselines, not full TCO. Annual cancellation, licence scope, support, operations, tax, increases, contingency and scope inclusions require confirmation. A's fixed-price offer is now evidenced, not its complete scope. F17 supersedes the earlier 0.9M build estimate for current costing; F18 supersedes the 2.5M cap. C's former 2.1M baseline excluded migration after support ends December 2028 and is not a live alternative.
Synthesis: A remains the conditional recommendation with stronger pricing-scale evidence; B remains over budget in both integration-cost readings, including with the nightly-import variant. Ana's earlier Composa preference remains hers to reconsider, not an assistant-overwritten decision.

# Draft recommendation — commerce platform for Northwind's spare parts shop
**DRAFT, updated 23 November 2026, for Ana's review.** For the December steering group; not agreed or selected. Evidence F1–F18 in page:91d008d5-bd21-4c24-8f28-2affcfeab4b7. Criteria weights remain unconfirmed. Fram commerce was dropped by Gunnar on 16 November because support ends December 2028 [F13].

## Recommendation
Take **Butikkskyen (A) forward as the preferred option, conditionally**. Do not recommend Composa (B) on current evidence. No weighted score or final selection is implied.

| | A. Butikkskyen | B. Composa |
|---|---|---|
| Build | Kodeverket fixed-price offer NOK 1.1m, valid until 15 December 2026 [F17]; scope/exclusions to check | NOK 1.8m estimate; whether NOK 0.8m integration is additional remains unresolved [F7,F11] |
| Three-year build + licence subtotal | NOK 2.45m = 1.1m + 3 × 0.45m, assuming one store [F12,F17] | NOK 4.5m–5.3m [F7,F11] |
| Year one vs new NOK 2.0m budget [F18] | NOK 1.55m; NOK 450,000 remains for unpriced costs | NOK 2.7m–3.5m; NOK 700,000–1.5m over budget |
| Speed | One reference live in four months [F9]. December decision + four months implies about April 2027, indicative only, not a delivery commitment | Four months integration before shop work [F11]; reference nine months with integration overrun [F10] |
| D365 | Included connector [F6]. Northwind's 3,100 price lists [F15] fall within vendor's stated v4 limit of 10,000; vendor says old workarounds unnecessary [F16]. Northwind demonstration still needed | Custom integration [F11]; capability and two-person team capacity unverified |
| Marketing in same tool | Unverified | Unverified |

A's cost, speed evidence and standard integration starting point support the conditional preference. F15–F16 remove the old 2,000-list threshold as a current stated product constraint, subject to validation. F17 supplies a fixed-price offer rather than an estimate, but not proof of full scope coverage. The smaller budget reduces room for extras. No option has demonstrated all requirements.

## Customer service
Hanne Ruud reports about 300 weekly calls about order status and prices combined and wants customer self-service order status [F14]. This establishes a need and baseline, not either platform's capability. Demonstrate authenticated order lookup, accurate customer-specific prices, and status for relevant orders (including phone/email-originated orders if required). Reordering and order-on-behalf remain unverified. Fewer calls is a plausible benefit, not a quantified saving; topic split, handling time and adoption are unknown. Customer service remains a separate section, not a scored criterion.

## Checks before commitment
1. **Commercial:** inspect Kodeverket's written scope and exclusions; confirm connector/app coverage, hosting, support, VAT, internal effort, one-store assumption and yearly cancellation. Use NOK 1.1m build, not the old NOK 0.9m estimate. Agree next steps before the offer expires on 15 December; seek an extension if the December decision is later.
2. **D365 and customer service:** demonstrate v4 with Northwind's 3,100 price lists, near-real-time prices and stock, customer-specific access and order status; validate performance and two-person team workload. Do not treat vendor capacity as an end-to-end test.
3. **Marketing and ordering:** task-based demonstration of same-tool content management, part-number ordering and quick reordering, for A and B.
4. **Delivery:** Kodeverket plan with mobilisation, dependencies and contingency to 1 September 2027. April 2027 is reference-based arithmetic only; obtain a second relevant reference if possible.

If integration or marketing checks fail, revisit the choice. Composa would also need a credible route inside the reduced budget, clarified integration scope/cost, team capacity and stronger delivery evidence.

## Steering-group decisions still needed
Confirm four-criterion weights (time to market, three-year cost, D365 fit, marketing ease); set a three-year cost ceiling; decide online-adoption targets and customer-service success measures. Subtotals are not full TCO. Ana's personal inclination towards Composa is separate from evidence.

## Comparison against the four current criteria — updated 23 November 2026
Current options A and B only. C (Fram commerce) was dropped on 16 November; earlier comparison remains in history. Design flexibility remains removed. Weights unagreed: no weighted scoring or final selection. Unknowns are not failures or successes.

| Criterion | A. Butikkskyen | B. Composa |
|---|---|---|
| Time to market | One reference live in four months [F9]; December decision implies about April 2027 by arithmetic only. Kodeverket delivery plan and capacity unconfirmed. Target 1 September 2027 [F1] | Reference nine months with integration overrun [F10]. Ola estimates four months custom integration before shop work [F11]; shop duration and achievable date unconfirmed |
| Three-year cost | NOK 2.45m = Kodeverket fixed build offer 1.1m [F17] + 3 × annual licence 0.45m [F12], assuming one store. Year one 1.55m, leaving 0.45m under new 2.0m budget [F18] before unpriced costs | NOK 4.5m = 1.8m build + 3 × 0.9m licence [F7], or 5.3m if Ola's 0.8m integration [F11] is extra. Year one 2.7m–3.5m, over new budget by 0.7m–1.5m |
| D365 fit | Standard connector and B2B Pricing app [F6]. Northwind has 3,100 price lists [F15]; vendor says v4 (October 2026) supports 10,000 without old reference workarounds [F16]. Supersedes the old 2,000-list concern for current-product assessment, not historical F9. Near-real-time prices/stock, performance and Northwind data untested | Custom integration required [F11]; no standard connector [F7]. Near-real-time prices/stock, customer pricing, feasibility and two-person team capacity remain unverified |
| Marketing ease | Same-tool workflow/usability unverified | Same-tool workflow/usability unverified |

**Interpretation:** Conditional draft preference remains A: lowest current subtotal, strongest positive speed evidence, included connector, now a reported fixed-price build offer and a stated capacity above Northwind's price-list count. B is over the reduced budget even if integration is included. No final choice; marketing and integration gates remain.

**Basis/limits:** Build plus three annual licence payments at unchanged rates. F17 replaces the older 0.9m A estimate in current calculations. The offer expires 15 December 2026. Neither subtotal is full TCO; scope, hosting, support, maintenance, internal effort, VAT and price changes unconfirmed. A assumes one store. Annual pricing does not establish yearly cancellation. Fixed build price does not fix all project costs. No three-year ceiling agreed.

**Validation gaps:** A: written offer scope/exclusions, one store, yearly cancellation, v4/D365 demonstration with 3,100 lists, delivery plan and marketing workflow. B: integration inside/on top of build, scope, capacity, second reference and route within budget. Both: part-number ordering, quick reorder, customer self-service order status and customer-specific data access. Customer service is separate from scored criteria; F14 adds a 300-calls/week baseline, not platform performance or savings evidence. Fram-specific questions retired from current recommendation.

## Customer-service implications — updated 23 November 2026
Separate section requested by Gunnar, not a new scored criterion.

**Evidence:** Hanne Ruud, head of customer service, reports about 300 weekly calls about order status and prices combined; the team wants customers to see order status themselves [F14]. Previously: 70% of orders arrive by email/phone [F5]; workshops want quick reordering [F2]. F14 supplies customer-service input but no vendor capability evidence.

**A. Butikkskyen:** v4's stated 10,000-list capacity covers Northwind's 3,100 in principle [F15,F16]. This is relevant to price accuracy at scale, not evidence of order-status self-service or reduced calls. Connector capability and status access remain to demonstrate.
**B. Composa:** self-service order lookup, reordering and order-on-behalf unverified. Custom D365 integration [F11] adds implementation risk; workload consequences are inference, not observed effects.
**C. Fram commerce:** dropped 16 November; no further assessment needed.

**Assumptions, not measured benefits:** accurate online prices and order status may reduce enquiries if customers adopt them. Inaccurate data may increase contacts. Do not treat all 300 calls as avoidable, or infer FTE/cost savings: no topic split, handling times or reduction rate supplied.

**Next validation:** with Hanne and vendors, demonstrate authenticated status lookup (clarify coverage of phone/email-originated orders), customer-specific prices, reorder and order-on-behalf; establish topic split and handling times; agree adoption and success measures with Gunnar. F14 closes the missing-interview-input gap but not the feature/workload gaps.

# Commerce platform recommendation — steering-group presentation outline
Draft, 23 November 2026. For the December steering group. Based on the updated recommendation item:9d1be4df-1c3d-4a65-9a6b-4f65fcdd8e2e and comparison item:21e8fa28-7f56-46b2-b275-3f1a60489577; findings F1–F18 in page:91d008d5-bd21-4c24-8f28-2affcfeab4b7. No platform selected; approval is requested, not recorded. Nine slides. Client-facing content names no other clients. Any distribution of pricing to Northwind must use its procurement portal, never email.

## 1. Recommendation: take Butikkskyen forward, subject to validation
- Preferred option on current evidence: lower quoted cost, strongest positive delivery evidence and included D365 connector.
- Do not recommend Composa on current evidence; it exceeds the reduced first-year budget.
- Conditional recommendation, not authority to sign before the checks are closed.

## 2. What the spare-parts shop must deliver
- About 4,000 parts; launch by 1 September 2027 [F1], distinct from website relaunch.
- Customer-specific prices and near-real-time D365 prices/stock; two-person integration team [F1,F3,F15].
- Same-tool marketing content, part-number ordering and quick reorder [F2,F5].
- Four criteria: time to market, three-year cost, D365 fit and marketing ease. Weights unagreed; no weighted score. Customer service assessed separately.

## 3. What the new findings change
- Hanne reports about 300 weekly calls about status and prices combined; wants self-service status [F14].
- Northwind has 3,100 price lists [F15]; vendor states B2B Pricing v4 supports 10,000 without former workarounds [F16]. Validate with Northwind data.
- Kodeverket fixed-build offer: NOK 1.1m, valid until 15 December 2026 [F17].
- First-year budget reduced from NOK 2.5m to NOK 2.0m [F18].

## 4. Cost: Butikkskyen fits the quoted scope; Composa is over budget
- Butikkskyen: NOK 1.1m build + NOK 0.45m annual licence; year one NOK 1.55m; three-year subtotal NOK 2.45m [F12,F17]. Assumes one store.
- NOK 450,000 remains under first-year ceiling, before unpriced costs—not confirmed contingency.
- Composa: year one NOK 2.7m–3.5m, exceeding budget by NOK 0.7m–1.5m; three-year subtotal NOK 4.5m–5.3m [F7,F11]. Range depends on whether integration is additional.
- Subtotals are not TCO. Confirm scope, hosting, support, VAT, internal effort, price changes and yearly cancellation. Three-year ceiling unagreed.

## 5. D365: stronger starting point for Butikkskyen, not yet proven
- Included connector and B2B Pricing app [F6]; 3,100 lists are within vendor's stated v4 capacity [F15,F16]. Old 2,000-list workaround concern is no longer a current stated constraint.
- Demonstrate near-real-time prices/stock, correct customer access and performance with Northwind data.
- Composa requires custom integration: Ola estimates NOK 800,000 and four months before shop work [F11]; scope, cost inclusion and team capacity unresolved.
- Same-tool marketing remains unverified for both; demonstrate it before commitment.

## 6. Delivery: April is an indication, September is the target
- One Butikkskyen reference went live in four months [F9]. December decision plus four months implies roughly April 2027, not a Northwind delivery commitment.
- Obtain Kodeverket's mobilisation, dependency, testing and contingency plan to 1 September 2027.
- Composa reference took nine months with integration overrun [F10]; four-month integration estimate adds schedule exposure, but is not an additive delivery forecast.
- Fram commerce was dropped on 16 November because support ends December 2028 [F13]; it is not a fallback under current analysis.

## 7. Customer service: a concrete need, benefits still to validate
- Baseline: about 300 weekly calls about status and prices combined [F14].
- Demonstrate authenticated order-status lookup, relevant order-channel coverage and accurate customer-specific prices; reorder/order-on-behalf remain unverified.
- Neither platform has demonstrated these service outcomes. Call reduction is plausible, not measured; do not equate 300 calls with avoidable calls or FTE savings.
- Agree adoption measures; obtain topic split and handling times before quantifying benefits. This is not a fifth scored criterion.

## 8. Four gates before contractual commitment
- Commercial: written fixed-price scope/exclusions, one-store assumption, full costs and yearly licence cancellation.
- Integration/service: v4 demonstration with 3,100 price lists, near-real-time D365 data, permissions and order status; confirm team capacity.
- Usability: marketing same-tool workflow, part-number ordering and quick reorder in task-based demos.
- Delivery: committed plan, dependencies and contingency; additional relevant reference if possible. If key gates fail, revisit recommendation rather than defaulting to Composa.

## 9. Decisions requested from the steering group
- Endorse Butikkskyen as preferred option for final validation; contract commitment only after gates pass.
- Confirm criterion weights and a three-year cost ceiling; retain NOK 2.0m first-year limit.
- Decide whether online-order adoption and customer-service targets are in scope, and assign owners for outstanding checks.
- Align decision/contract timing with 15 December offer expiry; seek an extension if checks or governance cannot finish in time.

texts.text:
**Butikkskyen remains the conditional preferred option—and the new findings strengthen its case.** I’ve saved F14–F18 and updated the comparison, customer-service section and draft recommendation privately.

First, I completed the carry-over: **a December decision plus the reference’s four-month implementation suggests roughly April 2027**. That is indicative arithmetic, not Kodeverket’s delivery commitment.

### Revised costs

| NOK million | Butikkskyen | Composa |
|---|---:|---:|
| Build + three years’ licences | **2.45** | **4.5–5.3** |
| First year | **1.55** | **2.7–3.5** |
| Against new **2.0m** budget | **0.45m remaining** | **0.7–1.5m over** |

Butikkskyen now uses Kodeverket’s **1.1m fixed-price offer**, replacing the earlier 0.9m estimate, plus 0.45m annual licensing. It still assumes one store. These are subtotals, not full project costs; the remaining 450,000 must cover any excluded costs.

### What changes
- **Price-list concern:** Northwind’s 3,100 lists fit within Butikkskyen’s stated v4 limit of 10,000. The old workaround concern is no longer a current stated product constraint—but performance and near-real-time D365 integration still need demonstrating.
- **Customer service:** We now have a concrete need and baseline: about **300 weekly calls about status and prices combined**. Neither option has yet demonstrated the required self-service. We cannot treat all 300 calls as avoidable or claim savings.
- **Commercial deadline:** The offer expires **15 December 2026**. I added a follow-up for 8 December to check scope, exclusions and decision timing, including an extension if needed.

**Before commitment:** validate D365/v4 with Northwind’s data, order-status self-service, marketing’s same-tool workflow, full costs/yearly cancellation, and Kodeverket’s delivery plan. No platform has been selected; criterion weights remain unagreed.

Updated records: [draft recommendation](item:9d1be4df-1c3d-4a65-9a6b-4f65fcdd8e2e), [comparison](item:21e8fa28-7f56-46b2-b275-3f1a60489577), [customer-service assessment](item:049c33a0-ecdc-4b52-a29d-dc26fd1823c8).

The [recommendation](item:9d1be4df-1c3d-4a65-9a6b-4f65fcdd8e2e) now incorporates F14–F18: **Butikkskyen remains preferred, subject to validation**, with revised costs, the v4 pricing capability, customer-service needs and the reduced budget.

## Steering-group presentation — 9-slide outline

### 1. Recommendation: take Butikkskyen forward conditionally
- Lowest quoted cost, strongest positive delivery evidence and an included Dynamics 365 connector.
- Composa is not recommended on current evidence: it exceeds the revised first-year budget.
- Seek endorsement of the preferred option—not unconditional authority to sign.

### 2. What the spare-parts shop must deliver
- About 4,000 parts; launch by **1 September 2027**.
- Customer-specific prices and near-real-time Dynamics 365 prices and stock.
- Same-tool content management for marketing, part-number ordering and quick reordering.
- Four assessment criteria: speed, three-year cost, D365 fit and marketing ease. Weights remain unagreed; customer service is assessed separately.

### 3. New findings strengthen the case—but tighten the constraints
- Customer service handles about **300 weekly calls about order status and prices combined**; customers should be able to check status themselves [F14].
- Northwind has **3,100 price lists**; Butikkskyen states that v4 supports **10,000** without the former workarounds [F15–F16].
- Kodeverket offers a **NOK 1.1m fixed-price build**, valid until **15 December 2026** [F17].
- First-year budget reduced to **NOK 2.0m** [F18].

### 4. Cost: Butikkskyen fits the quoted scope; Composa exceeds budget
| NOK million | Butikkskyen | Composa |
|---|---:|---:|
| First year | **1.55** | **2.7–3.5** |
| Three-year build + licences | **2.45** | **4.5–5.3** |
| Against 2.0m first-year budget | **0.45 remaining** | **0.7–1.5 over** |

- Butikkskyen assumes one store; Composa’s range depends on whether integration is additional.
- Subtotals are **not full TCO**. The NOK 450,000 remaining is not yet confirmed contingency.
- Confirm exclusions, support, hosting, VAT, internal effort and yearly cancellation.

### 5. D365: a stronger starting point, not yet proven
- Butikkskyen’s included connector and stated v4 capacity address the earlier price-list concern.
- Demonstrate performance, customer-specific access and near-real-time data with Northwind’s 3,100 lists.
- Composa needs custom integration: Ola estimates **NOK 800,000 and four months before shop work**.
- Marketing’s same-tool workflow remains unverified for both options.

### 6. Delivery: April is indicative; September is the target
- One Butikkskyen reference implemented in four months.
- A December decision therefore suggests roughly **April 2027**, but this is not a Northwind delivery commitment.
- Require Kodeverket’s mobilisation, dependencies, testing and contingency plan.
- Composa has greater schedule exposure. Fram commerce remains dropped because support ends in December 2028.

### 7. Customer service: a concrete need, benefits still unquantified
- Demonstrate authenticated order-status lookup and accurate customer-specific prices.
- Clarify whether status must cover orders placed by phone and email.
- Neither platform has demonstrated the required service outcomes.
- Do not treat all 300 calls as avoidable. Establish topic split, handling times and adoption measures before claiming savings.

### 8. Four gates before contractual commitment
- **Commercial:** fixed-price scope and exclusions, full costs, one-store assumption and yearly cancellation.
- **Integration and service:** D365/v4 demonstration, permissions, order status and team capacity.
- **Usability:** task-based tests of marketing content, part-number ordering and reordering.
- **Delivery:** credible plan with dependencies and contingency. Revisit the recommendation if key gates fail.

### 9. Decisions requested from the steering group
- Endorse Butikkskyen as preferred, subject to the four gates.
- Confirm criterion weights and a th

Added to slide 8, the risks/validation slide:

- **Third-party dependency:** the B2B Pricing app is a third-party dependency.

All other slides remain unchanged. [Saved amendment](item:9e3715f0-ac0b-4c0f-810b-a7ef093a5c98).

Saved a private [session record for 23 November](item:7c0c4aac-2e4b-4523-aba9-64fb80f32cb4), covering:

- **Worked on:** F14–F18, revised costs and recommendation, nine-slide outline, and the slide-8-only dependency addition.
- **Conclusion and why:** Butikkskyen remains conditionally preferred on cost, delivery evidence and integration starting point. No platform selected.
- **Still open:** commercial scope, demonstrations, delivery plan, criteria weights, full costs and adoption/service targets.
- **Next steps:** review the drafts, close the four validation gates and check Kodeverket’s offer before its **15 December expiry**. The **8 December follow-up** is saved.

The record points to the current drafts and the slide amendment so we can resume from here.

args.content:
# Commerce platform for Northwind's spare parts shop: research brief

Type: analysis brief
Status: updated **23 November 2026** with [F14–F18]. Preliminary comparison; weights, technical validation and contract scope remain open. [Draft recommendation](recommendation-draft.md): Butikkskyen, conditional, not an approved platform decision. **Decided 16 November: Fram commerce (C) is dropped.**

## What changed on 23 November 2026

- **Customer service:** Hanne Ruud reports about **300 calls a week about order status and prices**, and wants customers to see order status themselves [F14]. This is a combined call baseline, not 300 calls for each topic or a forecast of calls saved. Add customer-facing order-status demonstration to the evaluation.
- **Pricing scale:** Northwind has **3,100 customer-specific price lists** [F15]. Butikkskyen says B2B Pricing version 4, released in October, supports **up to 10,000 lists**, without the workarounds Agder Maskin needed [F16]. The old above-2,000-list caveat [F9] is superseded for version 4, not a current reason to reject A. Northwind is within the stated capacity, but performance, pricing correctness and connector behaviour still need validation.
- **Fixed-price build:** Kodeverket, Butikkskyen's partner, offers the build for **1.1m NOK fixed**, valid until **15 December 2026** [F17]. This replaces the earlier ~0.9m build estimate [F6] in the current comparison. Scope, exclusions, delivery and acceptance terms still need checking.
- **Budget cut:** management's first-year limit is now **2.0m NOK** [F18], replacing 2.5m [F1]. A's licence-and-build subtotal is **1.55m in year one**, leaving **0.45m** for unquoted costs, and **2.45m over three years** [F12, F17]. B remains about **3.5m in year one**, now **1.5m over budget** [F7, F11, F18].
- **Decision timing:** the December steering group date remains unknown. Confirm it immediately against the 15 December offer expiry. If approval and checks cannot finish in time, request an extension; do not assume either acceptance or an extension.

## Question and goals

Which commerce platform should Northwind use for its new spare parts shop? Gunnar Holm wants a recommendation for the steering group in December 2026; exact date and decision format remain unknown.

- Sell about 4,000 spare parts online to dealers and workshops; go live **1 September 2027** [F1].
- Speed to market matters most to Gunnar; marketing should manage shop content in the same tool as the website; workshops should reorder in a few clicks [F2].
- Customer service wants customers to see order status themselves [F14]. This is a newly evidenced functional need, not an agreed weighted criterion.

## Constraints and criteria

- Customer-specific prices [F1]; **3,100 customer-specific price lists** [F15]. Parts and price lists are different counts.
- Dynamics 365 holds prices and stock [F1]; all options must read these in near real time [F3]. Northwind's integration team has two people [F3].
- **First-year budget: 2.0m NOK** [F18], superseding the original 2.5m including licences and build [F1].
- Procurement wants fixed-price build and yearly-terminable licences [F4]. A now has a fixed-price build offer [F17]; annual termination is still unconfirmed.

Current criteria: **time to market, cost over three years, fit with Dynamics 365, ease of use for marketing** [F1; Ana's update, 9 November]. Weights are not agreed; Gunnar ranks speed first [F2]. No weighted scores assigned. Design flexibility was removed on 9 November because Gunnar says it does not matter. Historical reference comments on flexibility are not a basis for ranking.

Near-real-time prices/stock are mandatory; Dynamics fit measures effort to achieve this. Fixed price and annual termination, fast reorder, part-number ordering and customer-facing order status need explicit acceptance checks [F2–F5, F14]. Agree with Gunnar how these are treated as pass/fail requirements. Platform longevity beyond the three-year horizon is a suggested requirement, not yet agreed.

## Options and decision history

| | Option | Status |
|---|---|---|
| A | Butikkskyen: SaaS shop, partner build [F6]; Kodeverket fixed-price offer [F17] | Conditional preferred option, not approved. |
| B | Composa: headless engine; quoted build includes frontend [F7]; custom Dynamics integration needed [F11] | Not recommended on current cost and schedule evidence. |
| C | Fram CMS commerce module; marketing stays in Fram [F8] | **Dropped by agreement with Gunnar, 16 November 2026** (Ana's update), because support ends December 2028 [F13]. Not a candidate. |

Ana was leaning towards Composa on 9 November but worried about integration. Ola's subsequent estimate [F11] confirms additional cost and sequencing risk. The reason behind Ana's preference is not recorded; do not infer it.

## Comparison of the remaining options

Assessments are inferences from cited evidence, not vendor guarantees. Unknowns are not scored as failures.

| Criterion | A — Butikkskyen | B — Composa |
|---|---|---|
| Time to market | Strongest reference for speed: Agder Maskin live in four months [F9]. Included connector may reduce work [F6]. Counting four months from a December 2026 decision gives **April 2027**, early or late according to decision date, about four months before the deadline. This is reference-based arithmetic, not Northwind's delivery commitment. Confirm Kodeverket capacity, scope and dated plan. Offer expires 15 December [F17]. | Four months of integration **before shop work starts** [F11]. If begun in December, integration ends around April, leaving about five months for build and testing. Reference launched after nine months with integration overrun [F10]; nine months from December ends around September with no margin. Northwind shop duration is unquoted. |
| Cost over three years | **2.45m NOK** licence + build; **1.55m first year**, with **0.45m headroom** under current budget [F12, F17, F18]. Not full TCO. | **5.3m NOK** licence + build + integration; **3.5m first year**, **1.5m over budget** [F7, F11, F18], before unquoted costs. |
| Fit with Dynamics 365 | Standard connector and B2B Pricing app included [F6]. Northwind's 3,100 lists [F15] are within v4's vendor-stated 10,000 capacity; old workarounds no longer needed [F16]. Most promising evidence for lower effort; near-real-time behaviour, correctness and performance remain unproven. | No standard connector; custom integration estimated at 800,000 NOK and four months [F7, F11]. Reference integration overrun [F10]. High delivery/operations risk with a two-person integration team [F3]. Near-real-time capability unverified. |
| Ease of use for marketing | No demonstration of shop content managed in Fram, the website's tool [F2, F6]. Same-tool workflow remains a major gap. | Included frontend does not establish editorial workflow or Fram integration [F7]. Same-tool goal and usability unverified. |

### Cost basis and first-year budget

Million NOK; one build plus one or three annual licences, with B's integration added. Rates assumed unchanged. These are **subtotals, not complete total cost of ownership**. A's fixed price is subject to the offer's scope and validity; B's build and integration remain estimates.

| Cost | A — Butikkskyen [F6, F12, F17] | B — Composa [F7, F11] |
|---|---:|---:|
| Annual licence | 0.45 (one store) | 0.9 |
| Build, once | **1.1 fixed-price offer, valid to 15 December** | ~1.8 |
| Dynamics 365 integration | Standard connector included in licence; additional implementation scope to confirm | ~0.8, Ola's estimate |
| First year | **1.55** | **~3.5** |
| Headroom against **2.0m** budget [F18] | **0.45** | **1.5 over budget** |
| Three years | **2.45** | **~5.3** |

- A assumes one store at 450,000 NOK annually [F12]. Confirm Northwind needs only one, and that Kodeverket's fixed scope includes all required implementation, integrations, workflows and testing. Version 4 removes the old price-list workarounds [F16]; it does not prove all integration work is cost-free.
- A's build is 0.2m higher than the old estimate [F6, F17]. Combined with the 0.5m budget cut, headroom falls from the previous 1.15m to **0.45m**. The previous 1.35m/2.25m A subtotals are superseded.
- B's 0.8m integration is treated as additional to the 1.8m build because no standard connector is quoted [F7, F11]. Confirm overlap and who delivers it.
- Clarify hosting, maintenance, support, internal effort, upgrades, transaction fees, tax basis, price escalation and contingency. None is quantified. A is below budget on known items, **not yet proven within budget overall**.
- Annual pricing does not establish yearly termination rights [F4]. A's fixed-price offer resolves the existence of an offer, not its scope or all procurement terms. B's fixed-price terms are unconfirmed.

**Historical C costs, not a current alternative:** annual module 0.3m; build ~1.2m; first year ~1.5m plus unknown integration; three-year subtotal ~2.1m plus integration and replatforming [F8, F13]. Support ends December 2028, about 15 months after planned launch. The subtotal excludes the necessary platform move, so it is not comparable to A/B. No further C commerce evaluation is needed; check only whether the website CMS itself is affected.

## Requirements and evidence gaps

- **Near-real-time prices and stock:** not demonstrated for either option. Ola should validate latency, load, failure handling and operational ownership at Northwind's volume [F3]. Connector/API availability is not proof.
- **Customer-specific prices:** count is resolved: 3,100 [F15]. Butikkskyen's v4 claim resolves the old stated capacity/workaround concern [F16], but validate version deployed, list complexity, price correctness, permissions, refresh behaviour and performance using Northwind data. B's pricing support at this scale remains unverified.
- **Reorder and part-number ordering:** not demonstrated [F2, F5]. Dealers mostly order by part number; 70% of orders currently arrive by email and phone [F5]. Ask Cara whether history, saved lists, part-number entry or upload best supports users.
- **Order status:** demonstrate customer-facing visibility, status data source, update timing and access controls [F14]. Dynamics is known to hold prices and stock [F1]; the order-status source and integration coverage are not yet established.
- **Contracts and delivery:** get scoped delivery plans, yearly termination terms, and verify the written Kodeverket offer before its 15 December expiry [F4, F17]. Reference durations are not commitments.
- **Roadmap:** ask A and B for support commitments, given Fram's end-of-support announcement [F13].

## Option B (Composa) revisited

B does not currently fit the constraints:

- **Budget:** ~3.5m first year against **2.0m** [F7, F11, F18]. Licence plus integration already consumes 1.7m, leaving only **0.3m** for a quoted ~1.8m build, before other costs. A reduced scope, changed integration economics or explicit budget change would be needed; none is agreed.
- **Schedule:** as of 23 November there are a little over nine months to 1 September 2027. Four months of integration precedes shop work [F11]. A December start leaves little margin against the reference's nine-month total [F10]; Northwind build duration is unknown.
- **Delivery risk:** custom integration, a two-person Northwind team [F3], unknown delivery/operations owner, and no fixed integration price [F4, F11].
- **Benefit in return:** the reference's flexibility [F10] is no longer a criterion. B has no demonstrated lead on the four remaining criteria; marketing remains unknown for both.
- **What could reopen B:** a supported connector or fixed-price plan that materially cuts cost and duration, an explicitly approved budget/date change, or relevant evidence behind Ana's earlier preference. Do not assume management will reverse the budget cut.

This is an evidence-based recommendation, not a platform decision. Gunnar and the steering group decide.

## What each option means for customer service

Requested by Gunnar on 9 November; **not an agreed weighted criterion**. Baseline now includes direct evidence, not only inference:

- 70% of orders arrive by email and phone [F5]. This is an order-channel share, not a measured customer-service workload or savings figure.
- Hanne Ruud, head of customer service, reports about **300 calls per week about order status and prices combined**, and wants customer self-service order status [F14]. The split between topics, handling time and achievable reduction are unknown.

**Potential effects (inference):** correct customer-specific prices and usable order-status visibility could reduce some calls; easy online reorder could reduce manual order entry. No vendor has demonstrated these outcomes and no savings target is agreed. Login, price discrepancies or stale status could create new support work.

| | A — Butikkskyen | B — Composa |
|---|---|---|
| Potential implications | Earlier likely launch could bring relief sooner [F9], if self-service functions work. Version 4 removes the old price-list workarounds according to vendor [F16]; do not carry forward the old scale-risk argument. Correctness and live performance still need testing. | Custom integration and the reference's integration overrun add delivery risk [F10, F11]. Self-service benefits could arrive later; actual support burden is unquantified. |
| Unknown | Customer-facing order-status capability and source; admin/order lookup; customer-view pricing; ordering on behalf of customers; status integration within Kodeverket scope. | Same customer-service capabilities; status source/integration; who maintains custom integration. |

C is dropped. Historically a second platform move after launch would have meant another customer experience/support change [F13]; no further C demonstration is needed.

**Next:** Hanne should help define and test customer order-status and price-visibility scenarios with Ola and the vendors. Establish call split and success measures before estimating savings. Check customer-service admin workflows separately from customers' own status visibility.

## Interim view

**Butikkskyen remains the conditional preferred option.** Its speed reference and standard Dynamics route fit Gunnar's priority [F2, F6, F9]. The new pricing evidence removes the obsolete above-2,000-list objection: 3,100 is within the vendor-stated v4 capacity [F15, F16]. Kodeverket provides a fixed-price build offer [F17]. However, **0.45m first-year headroom is not a complete affordability conclusion**, and order status, marketing workflow, technical performance, scope and annual termination still need checking.

Composa is now about 1.5m over the reduced budget, with its integration sequencing still putting launch at risk [F7, F11, F18]. C remains dropped. The recommendation is conditional, not an approved selection or a final weighted ranking. The April 2027 A estimate remains reference-based, not a delivery promise.

## Open questions and next steps

1. **Urgent — Gunnar/Lise:** when is the December meeting, who approves and in what format? Can approval and validation finish before **15 December**? If not, seek a written extension from Kodeverket; do not assume one [F17].
2. Agree weights for the four criteria with Gunnar and acceptance checks for self-service order status, marketing, reorder and pricing. Discuss platform longevity.
3. **Lise/Kodeverket:** obtain and review the fixed-price scope, exclusions, milestones, acceptance, support and payment terms. Confirm implementation of order status, v4 pricing and Fram workflow, and yearly licence termination [F4, F17].
4. **Cost:** complete the first-year and three-year operating-cost picture. Test all extras and contingency against A's **0.45m** headroom [F18]. Confirm one-store licence scope [F12].
5. **Ola/Butikkskyen:** validate v4 against the known **3,100 lists**, including complexity, load and correctness; validate near-real-time prices/stock and operational ownership [F3, F15, F16]. Count is resolved; complexity and performance remain open.
6. **Hanne/vendors:** demonstrate customer-facing order status and price visibility. Establish status source, update timing and permissions; separately demonstrate service-team lookup and on-behalf ordering. Clarify call mix and intended measures [F14].
7. **Kodeverket:** obtain a dated plan from a December decision through testing and launch. Test the reference-based April estimate and confirm capacity [F9, F17].
8. **Marketing/vendors:** demonstrate same-tool content management alongside Fram for A and B [F2]. Check whether the website's known API limit of 10 requests a second matters if the shop reads Fram content/data (see website relaunch page).
9. **Composa:** confirm integration/build overlap, delivery owner, fixed-price possibilities and a dated plan including the four-month integration [F11]. Seek a second reference, focusing on integration overruns [F10]. Who builds/runs the frontend, and how does it support Fram editorial work?
10. **Cara/vendors:** test reorder and part-number flows [F2, F5]. Is moving a defined share of phone/email orders online a goal? Do not conflate the 70% order-channel share with the 300 status/price calls.
11. **Fram:** no further commerce evaluation; check only whether the website CMS is affected by commerce-module end of support [F13]. Ask A/B for roadmap commitments.
12. Ana: add the reason for the earlier Composa preference if still relevant; review the [draft recommendation](recommendation-draft.md) before sharing with Gunnar.

## Sources

- Ana's update, 9 November 2026: Gunnar removed design flexibility as a criterion and requested customer service implications. Ana leaned towards Composa but was concerned about integration; Ola was checking it.
- Ana's update, 16 November 2026: Gunnar agreed to drop Fram commerce because support ends in 2028; Ana requested an A go-live estimate counting four months from a December decision.
- [F1] Kickoff notes, 28 October 2026 (Ana): about 4,000 parts; 1 September 2027 go-live; customer-specific prices; Dynamics 365; original first-year budget 2.5m NOK (superseded by F18).
- [F2] Interview with Gunnar Holm, 29 October 2026: speed first; same-tool marketing content; quick reorder.
- [F3] Interview with Ola Nordmann, integration architect, 29 October 2026: near-real-time prices/stock; two-person integration team.
- [F4] Interview with Lise Berg, procurement, 30 October 2026: fixed-price build and yearly-terminable licences.
- [F5] Market note from Cara, 30 October 2026: dealers mostly order by part number; 70% of orders arrive by email and phone.
- [F6] Butikkskyen quote, 3 November 2026: annual licence 600,000 NOK (corrected by F12); partner build ~900,000 NOK (superseded by F17); standard Dynamics connector and B2B Pricing app included in licence.
- [F7] Composa quote, 4 November 2026: annual licence 900,000 NOK; build ~1.8m including frontend; no standard Dynamics connector, integration through API.
- [F8] Fram CMS quote, 4 November 2026: commerce module 300,000 NOK annually; build ~1.2m; marketing stays in Fram.
- [F9] Agder Maskin reference call, 5 November 2026: live in four months; B2B Pricing worked but needed workarounds above 2,000 lists. Historical limitation superseded for v4 by F16; speed reference remains relevant.
- [F10] Vestlandsdeler reference call, 6 November 2026: Composa very flexible; nine-month launch; integration overran.
- [F11] Ola Nordmann, 11 November 2026: Composa custom Dynamics integration estimated at 800,000 NOK and four months before shop work starts.
- [F12] Butikkskyen correction, 12 November 2026: 600,000 NOK was for two stores; one store is 450,000 NOK annually.
- [F13] Fram CMS, 12 November 2026: commerce-module support ends December 2028; recommends partner platform migration.
- [F14] Hanne Ruud, head of customer service, 17 November 2026: about 300 calls weekly about order status and prices; wants customers to see order status themselves.
- [F15] Ola Nordmann, 18 November 2026: Northwind has 3,100 customer-specific price lists.
- [F16] Butikkskyen, 19 November 2026: B2B Pricing v4, released in October, handles up to 10,000 lists; Agder Maskin's workarounds no longer necessary.
- [F17] Lise Berg, 19 November 2026: Butikkskyen partner Kodeverket offers build at fixed price 1.1m NOK, valid until 15 December.
- [F18] Gunnar Holm, 20 November 2026: management cut first-year budget to 2.0m NOK.

Related: [Northwind](../overview.md), [Website relaunch](../website-relaunch/website-relaunch.md), [Gunnar Holm](../website-relaunch/gunnar-holm.md), [Lise Berg](../website-relaunch/lise-berg.md)
